newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Offshore baht up on fund shortage.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Offshore baht up on fund shortage.

text.p: The Thai baht surged in offshore markets on Wednesday as a continued funding squeeze forced players to sell dollars to cover short positions.

Dealers said the baht went to a high of 24.30 against the dollar as U.S. investment houses and life insurance companies unwound long dollar/baht positions established before the Bank of Thailand (BOT)'s defence of the baht against speculators.
"A lot of people took long dollar/baht positions during the crisis and they didn't expect the central bank to create this two-tier market," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
She said offshore players were being forced to cut these positions as soaring swaps, due to a shortage of baht funds, made them too expensive to fund.
"Any rally in the dollar towards 24.85/90 will be a sell," she said. Players would prefer to stay out of the market altogether as spreads quoted were very wide, she added.
The baht was quoted at 25.850/25.855 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 24.500/24.600 early and 24.670/24.770 late on Tuesday. In domestic markets, the baht was at 25.850/855.
The BOT set the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.82 against 25.84 on Tuesday.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded around 140/155 satangs per dollar offshore and 20/30 onshore.

In Malaysia, the ringgit was under pressure from rumours of a large trade deficit for April, but dealers said fears of central bank support for the currency would confine its downside to 2.5200 to the dollar for the time being.
"The market is talking about a one- to two-billion-ringgit deficit for April and this will continue to pressure the ringgit," a dealer at a large Malaysian bank said.
Malaysia posted a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March.
Dealers said the market was also awaiting April monetary supply figures, which could provide some clues to the country's interest rate direction.
"There are some sellers (of the dollar) at 2.5190 and that's capping it temporarily. But if it breaks, we could see 2.5250 and 2.5340," the Singapore dealer said.
The Singapore dollar continued to trade in a range, benefitting slightly from the unwinding of long ringgit/Sing positions by U.S. funds near the 0.5700 resistance.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was steady but showed signs of rising further against the dollar after last week's general elections proceeded relatively smoothly.
Dealers said a mixed set of economic figures had little immediately effect on the rupiah, with low inflation in May offsetting a drop in the March trade surplus.
However, the rupiah remained supported at the 2,426 level.
Spot rupiah was at 2,426.5/27.5 at 0425 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.0/28.0.
A Jakarta state bank dealer said there were some attempts to push the rupiah above the 2,426.0 level but corporate dollar purchases helped cap its rise.
"I think it's just a question of time when we will see the rupiah test the 2,425.0 level, if there is no further trouble in the post-election week," the dealer said.
Many players remained cautious about possible unrest if the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) decided to reject the election results.
The party has alleged there were widespread irregularities during last week's election and said it would decide on Thursday whether to accept the results.
Dealers said tighter money market liquidity also helped support the rupiah, with overnight money traded at around 12.0 percent on Wednesday morning.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik
